facts.value: Internet addiction disorder (IAD), also called problematic Internet use (PIU), is characterized by excessive or poorly controlled preoccupations, urges, or behaviors regarding computer use and Internet access that lead to impairment or distress.
facts.programme_association: Social Sciences - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: There is concern that increased access to the Internet among young people may cause students' academic performance to decline.
facts.programme_association: Social Sciences - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Some experience health consequences from loss of sleep as they stay up to continue scrolling, chatting, and gaming.
facts.programme_association: Social Sciences - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Excessive Internet use is not recognized as a disorder by the American Psychiatric Association's DSM-5 or the World Health Organization's ICD-11.
facts.programme_association: Social Sciences - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Controversy around the diagnosis includes whether the disorder is a separate clinical entity, or a manifestation of other underlying psychiatric disorders.
facts.programme_association: Social Sciences - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Many different theoretical models have been developed and employed for many years in order to better explain predisposing factors to this disorder.
facts.programme_association: Social Sciences - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Models such as the cognitive-behavioral model of pathological Internet have been used to explain IAD for more than 20 years.
facts.programme_association: Social Sciences - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Newer models, such as the Interaction of Person-Affect-Cognition-Execution model, have been developed more recently and are starting to be applied in more clinical studies.
facts.programme_association: Social Sciences - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: In 2011 the term 'Facebook addiction disorder' (FAD) emerged.
facts.programme_association: Social Sciences - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: FAD is characterized by compulsive use of Facebook.
facts.programme_association: Social Sciences - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: A 2017 study investigated a correlation between excessive use and narcissism, reporting 'FAD was significantly positively related to the personality trait narcissism and to negative mental health variables (depression, anxiety, and stress symptoms)'.
facts.programme_association: Social Sciences - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Studies have shown that there has been an increase in the prevalence of IAD since the COVID-19 pandemic.
facts.programme_association: Social Sciences - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Studies highlighting the possible relationship between COVID-19 and IAD have looked at how forced isolation and its associated stress may have led to higher usage levels of the Internet.
facts.programme_association: Social Sciences - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: A study involving 157 online learners on massive open online courses examined the impact of turning off social media notifications to help reduce social media use.
facts.programme_association: Social Sciences - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: The study reported that providing support in self-regulation was associated with a reduction in time spent online, particularly on entertainment.
facts.programme_association: Social Sciences - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Research suggests that social media platforms trigger a cycle of compulsive behavior, which reinforces addictive patterns and makes it harder for individuals to break the cycle.
facts.programme_association: Social Sciences - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Various lawsuits have been brought regarding social media addiction, such as the Multi-District Litigation alleging harms caused by social media addiction on young users.
facts.programme_association: Social Sciences - BSc | University of Limerick
